result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely compromised by a large accumulation of debris and trash that completely obstructs the sidewalk. The lack of maintenance and absence of safety infrastructure force pedestrians to walk in the roadway, significantly increasing risk.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large pile of trash, furniture, and debris completely blocks the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image on the sidewalk area.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk and road surface are cracked and uneven, creating trip hazards.

interventions.title: Debris Removal
interventions.description: Clear the sidewalk of all obstructions to restore a safe, continuous walking path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk surface to provide a safe, ADA-compliant walking path.

result.summary: The street environment consists of a two-lane roadway with parking on both sides and sidewalks present but lacking safety enhancements. There are no marked crosswalks or traffic calming measures visible, and parked vehicles create significant sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, requiring pedestrians to cross the roadway without clear priority or markings.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both curbs block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to enter the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential intersection with significant sidewalk obstructions and faded infrastructure. While the low-speed nature of the narrow street is a positive, the presence of a trailer blocking the walkway and poor sightlines at the corner create hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large trailer and construction debris completely block the sidewalk on the right corner, forcing pedestrians into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and mid-ground sidewalk area

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Overgrown vegetation and the parked trailer at the corner block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crossing.

hazards.name: Faded Pavement Markings
hazards.description: The crosswalk and stop bar markings are heavily worn and difficult to see, reducing driver awareness of the crossing.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance
interventions.description: Remove the trailer and debris from the sidewalk to restore a continuous, accessible path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the faded transverse markings with a high-visibility ladder or zebra pattern.

interventions.title: Corner Daylighting
interventions.description: Clear vegetation and implement parking/storage restrictions near the corner to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standardized curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to ensure the crossing is accessible.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure and severely degraded sidewalks on one side of the street. The presence of debris and overgrown vegetation on the right walkway forces pedestrians into the roadway, while parked vehicles on the left further restrict visibility and space.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction and Debris
hazards.description: The right-side sidewalk is covered in trash, debris, and broken pavement, making it impassable for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and mid-ground along the brick building

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross the two-lane road without designated space or priority.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street block sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Clear debris and repave the sidewalk on the right side to provide a continuous, accessible walking path.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking near potential crossing points to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.
